description: Roughly 158,000 refugees who fled Gaza to Jordan after June 1967, per UNRWA. They were never given Jordanian citizenship and remain stateless. During Egypt's control of Gaza they had Egyptian travel documents but not Egyptian citizenship.
energy_note: Stateless in the country they've lived in since 1967.

description: A temporary passport valid two years, with no national ID number. It is in effect a residency permit renewable at the state's discretion, and renewal runs through the Ministry of Interior with the prime minister's approval.
money_note: Renewal costs, every two years, for life.
energy_note: Reapplying to exist, every twenty-four months.

aspect: The missing number is the whole problem
description: Without a national number there are no political rights, no social security, and restricted job access. The document permits presence and little else.

aspect: Several states will not honour it
description: Syria, Lebanon, Egypt and some Gulf states are among those refusing to recognise the document. It is a travel document that does not reliably travel.
energy_note: A passport that is not accepted in the neighbouring country.

description: Any delay in the two-year renewal risks leaving the holder with no valid status at all. An administrative backlog becomes an immigration offence.
energy_note: Illegal because an office was slow.

aspect: You may not hold both documents
description: Jordan does not permit stateless Palestinians to hold both a Jordanian temporary passport and a PA passport, so acquiring one may cost the other. Canada's IRB has examined whether taking a PA passport forfeits Jordanian rights entirely.
energy_note: Two weak documents, and you may only have one.

description: Gazans are treated separately from other Palestinians in Jordan and must identify a guarantor to enter. A person without a well-placed contact does not travel.
energy_note: You need someone to vouch for you to go home.

description: Gazans are treated separately from other Palestinians in Jordan and must identify a guarantor in order to enter. A person without a well-placed contact in the country does not travel, regardless of what their documents say.
energy_note: You need someone respectable to vouch for your existence.
